picks.why: The growers' co-operative founded at Paarl in 1918 that governed the Cape's wine trade for seventy years; The Mentors is the range its own pages call its flagship collection, and Perold, its Cape Blend with Pinotage, honours the creator of Pinotage, who worked for KWV.

Abraham Izak Perold carries his dates (1880 to 1941) only from two sources. No volume or size claim. Roodeberg and the fortified wines of the Boberg tradition belong in others.

picks.why: Paarl Mountain farm of the Back family, whose own label dates from 1974, known for Shiraz and the Rhône grapes; Cyril Back, named for a past head of the family, is the house's flagship red, Shiraz led in the vintages read.

picks.why: Estate of 1985 on the northern slopes of the Simonsberg in the Paarl district; Quartz Stone, a single vineyard Chardonnay named for the quartz in its soil, is one of its pair of flagships beside the Gravel Quarry Cabernet Sauvignon.

picks.why: The co-operative of 1941 at the foot of the Paardeberg, the voice of the district's dry farmed bush vine Chenin Blanc; the Courageous, a barrel fermented Chenin of its Dryland Collection, is the wine that carries its Chenin into the competitions.

picks.why: Franschhoek house on a farm dating to 1776, its modern winery re-established in 1993; its Syrah, grown on cooler sites outside the valley, is one of the wines that turned Cape red towards a fresher, peppery style.
picks.note: The library holds the house and the Syrah. Confirm the Syrah's source and the Wine of Origin its label carries, since the library warns that the house's address and the fruit's origin differ. The founding winemaker is living (in people.json): never named. Porseleinberg, wave one's Swartland pick, is the house's Swartland farm by the region record: a different house and wine, so say so. The old vine Franschhoek Sémillon and The Chocolate Block belong in others.

picks.why: Franschhoek house on land granted to the Huguenot Pierre Jourdan on 22 December 1694; its Cap Classique wines carry his name and its still wines the estate's, and Pierre Jourdan Brut, from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, is the sparkling wine the house was founded on.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the first release (1984 and 1986 are both told) and the claim of a first Cap Classique wholly from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, hedged as the house's. The founder's death in December 2025 is reported by one source only: name him with dates only from two sources, else say the founder. Name no living member of the family. The founder had made sparkling wine at Boschendal, this group's other pick, before.

picks.why: The Groot Drakenstein estate founded in 1685, among the Cape's oldest, known for Chardonnay, Shiraz and Cap Classique; Grande Cuvée Brut is the bottle fermented wine of the house.

picks.why: A Huguenot-named farm of the late seventeenth century in the valley, known for Shiraz and Sauvignon Blanc and for its arts and gardens; the Pierneef wines are named for the landscape painter whose work the estate shows.

picks.why: A portion of Simon van der Stel's Constantia estate of 1685; Vin de Constance, the unfortified Muscat de Frontignan revived with the 1986 vintage, is the modern answer to the sweet wine that reached Europe's courts.
picks.note: The library holds the house (p-klein-constantia) and the wine (w-vin-de-constance) and leaves the house's founding year empty: keep it empty unless two sources agree. Simon van der Stel carries his dates (1639 to 1712) from two sources. The 500 millilitre bottle copies the antique: confirm the story from two sources. Name no living owner or winemaker.

picks.why: The original estate of 1685 and the Cape's oldest wine farm, bought by Hendrik Cloete in 1778, whose sweet wine reached Europe's courts; Grand Constance, unfortified and amber from red and white Muscat de Frontignan, is the estate's own revival of it.
